newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Six Nicaraguan soldiers killed in ambush.
newsitem.headline: Six Nicaraguan soldiers killed in ambush.

text.p: Six Nicaraguan soldiers were killed and four injured on Thursday in an ambush in a remote part of central Nicaragua a day before President-elect Arnoldo Aleman was to take office, an army spokesman said.

The army has not identified the attackers and has sent troops to the region, located 11 miles (18 kms) northeast of the town of Rio Blanco in the department (province) of Matagalpa, Capt. Milton Sandoval told Reuters.
Confirmed dead are Maj. Roberto Flores Siles, Capt. Ramon Mendoza Morales and Capt. Walter Castro Olivas, plus three soldiers, he said.
Aleman will assume the presidency on Friday with about 400 members of armed bands still operating in remote parts of north and central Nicaragua, according to army estimates.

Many of the rebels are descendants of the former U.S.-backed Contra rebels or former Sandinsta army who re-armed after Nicaragua's 1990 peace agreement, unhappy with the government's failure to fulfil the terms of treaties ending an eight-year civil war.
The new government has said it plans to begin negotiating a demobilization with some of the main armed bands on Jan. 15.
